recs.name: A Plan
recs.tag: It may be an overgrown ruins, but it'll still catch the warm gaze of the setting sun.

lines.x: Open the door, you lousy scammer!
Open the damn door!
I know you're there! Open this blasted door already!
Good morning, Mr. Haller. You shouldn't be so loud; it'll disturb the others, you know.
(Grabs Totter by the collar)
Do you take me for a fool, you son of a bitch?!
You said you'd have it done by Friday! It's Friday, and all you've done is pack up and get ready to leave!
Patience, my friend. I'll explain afterwards.
(Pulls away Haller's hand)
Explain? I don't need a goddamn explanation. I need results, you understand? I need the heads of those bastards on a platter, now.
(Glances at watch) Just give me a little more time.
You said five days. I gave you five days. What now?
The plan is going well. You'll have your results soon enough.
Plan? What have you been doing the past four days?
You drank coffee on Monday, played poker on Tuesday, went to the market on Wednesday, and slept through Thursday. Now it's Friday, and you haven't even moved your ass one inch from your room.
(Glances at watch)
Stop looking at your goddamn watch!
It’s not time yet.
What? Are you telling me to calm down?
...I guess so?
Easy for you to say, you son of a bitch! It wasn't you who lost everything to those bandits!
Oh, believe me, I could tell how little you had left by the amount you were offering.
...Yeah, if I had any left over, you'd be worrying about your own head instead of anyone else's.
My, and here I thought we had a good partnership going.
(Slumps against the wall)
I should've died along with my wife... At least then I wouldn't have to deal with this shit.
Would you like some hot water? I can get you a cup.
You—forget it. Why should I talk to you about it? You don't know how I feel.
Not quite... I do know, to an extent.
Then do something. I'm begging you.
(Glances at watch)
(Shakes head) *Sigh*...
It's time. Would you like to come with me?
For what?
Blood for blood, just like you asked.
Here we are. Have you hidden your burdenbeast?
Yes... Wait, why are you the one giving the orders, when I'm the one hiring you?
My apologies, Mr. Haller. Would you like me to go tie it up again?
No need. I'd rather you explained why you brought me all the way out here.
Take these.
Binoculars?
Look over there.
I don't see anything.
Further. There's a convoy coming towards us from the horizon, flying blood-red flags with black skulls on them.
I see it! It's them! It's them!
(Draws crossbow)
You don't need binoculars?
No.
But it's so far away.
Shh. Quiet.
Done.
So quick?
Yeah... Unless there was something else?
What?
I mean, I'm not too keen on desecrating corpses, but if you insist...
You... you're sure there are no survivors?
By the size of the explosion, I would say the odds are slim.
They're dead. They're all dead. Good.
You don't sound as happy as I expected.
I thought I would be, but... it all happened so quick. Almost like it wasn't real.
Now, maybe this isn't the best time to bring this up, but as for the other half...
(Tosses out a bag of gold coins)
Take it.
(Picks up the bag)
Don't you have anything to say?
...Thank you for your business?
Those eggheads spent a month trying to track that group down and came up empty-handed. How did you do it?
How did you know they would show up right here, right now?
Actually...
Ach, let's talk someplace else. I need a stiff drink.
I wouldn't recommend drinking in your current state.
Ha... what would you know about it?
Apparently, the people in this town drink in the morning to celebrate the sunrise. I ordered two drinks. Which one do you want?
They're not exactly the same size.
Yeah, the big one's mine.
Why did you ask me to choose, then?
To be polite.
I'll take the small one then, thank you.
(Guzzles half the mug)
Argh—burp.
So can you talk now? How did you do it? You didn't prepare anything the last few days. You just showed up there, pulled back your crossbow, and whoosh—
They're gone.
What the hell was that? Future sight? Did you bribe one of them?
Come on, tell me. I just don't understand. I was sure you were scamming me when I found you last night, but now...
Let's just say that if you wanted me to lick your boots, I'd get on my knees this instant.
You're getting a little too excited.
I've had something to drink.
It wasn't so hard. It's all about having a good plan, and following it step by step.
(Takes out a notebook)
You complained that I spent all Monday in a cafe, but the cafe in this town plays an important role.
It's sort of an information exchange for traders passing through.
It's where all the news spreads, true or false.
Have you managed to get your spices out? I've tried other routes, but it seemed like they always knew where we were going.
Still thinking about what to do. I might just throw my hands up and hire mercenaries to guard the goods. Better than letting it rot in the warehouse.
When is the lord ameer going to do something about this? I can't afford any more losses.
Hello, what can I get for you?
A cup of coffee, please.
Our coffee is strong by most places' standards, so it comes with a plate of honey dates to balance out the bitterness.
Thank you. I like my coffee bitter anyway.
By the way, could I ask where the town doctor lives?
The east side of town. Just head east along the fountain. Are you ill?
I have a batch of emergency medical supplies that I thought might come in useful for somebody.
Medicine, not money, is the most powerful currency in the barrenlands. Now that the cat was out of the bag, I had to prove I was worth the trip.
I think my luck's about to change.
Time to cut your losses, buddy. Your wife isn't gonna like it when she finds out how much you've lost.
Eh, it's just some spare change. I play for the thrill.
Ha, that's what we like to hear!
One more round! Let's go!
I found footprints outside my window Wednesday morning, as expected. Someone tried to cover them up, but it was the work of an amateur.
Have you ever hunted, Mr. Haller?
Wild animals have their own territory, and they follow certain rules when they look for food or wander around in it. Understand their habits, and you'll know where to place your traps.
Leaving so soon, sir?
Yes, I'm concerned about these bandits I keep hearing about. The sooner I can leave, the better.
Do you know of any other routes out of here?
To be honest with you, sir, it makes little difference whichever route you pick. They know every move you're about to make, and there's no way to avoid their ambushes.
Have you all been attacked before, then?
My convoy tried leaving by a tiny trail to the east, but the bastards were laying in wait an hour out from town.
That's terrifying. Has anyone managed to avoid them?
We tried many different routes, big and small, but it makes no difference. You're doomed to run into them no matter what.
I identified where the bandits operated by comparing the convoy routes to the locations where they encountered the outlaws.
I found a few sniping vantage points, from which my crossbow could cover those areas.
The final step was to lure my prey into the trap.
Hey, kid, wanna make some quick cash?
What do you want, sir?
I'm leaving town tomorrow. Get me ten days' worth of fresh water and dry rations, and have my burdenbeast fed before sunset. I'll be leaving before dawn.
Here are four gold coins for your trouble. I'll be waiting at the west entrance at 5 a.m. tomorrow.
Wow! You've got it, sir.
Now get going, and don't disturb me. I need to sleep before the trip.
No problem, sir. I'll get it done!
Two gold coins would have been a fair price, but I paid him twice that.
A kid that age can't help but brag when he runs into a stroke of luck. And the more people he tells, the better.
So you weren't sleeping yesterday?
No, I slept. Needed to be in top form for what was to come.
(Takes a gulp)
So... that's what happened.
You sound disappointed.
Yeah... I thought I'd hear the breathtaking story of a legendary mercenary, but it ended up being more like one of my wife's business proposals: detailed, but boring.
A good plan doesn't need twists and turns. The safer it is, the better.
That's what she said, too! She even had a notebook with her at all times, just like you.
It's a good habit to have. People shouldn't trust their own memories. So what's she doing now?
The bandits cut off her head... I told you that when I first came to you.
...Oh, right. Sorry.
It's okay. At least she doesn't have to worry about writing any more business proposals. She'd probably have been a poet, if I hadn't dragged her into my business.
Yes, poet is a good occupation. Safe.
To be totally frank with you, chatting with you makes me uncomfortable.
I get that a lot. I'm just grateful to those who are satisfied with merely saying so. Plenty more wouldn't leave it at that.
My brain tells me I should say something comforting, but my heart would never let me.
Sorry.
(Shakes head) Never mind.
Can I take a look at your notebook?
Sure.
Your writing is really big.
I have something of an eye problem. I can see things far away perfectly, but things that are up close, not so much.
Looks like you meticulously plan out everything in life.
Yes. Having a plan in place makes things less hectic when trouble comes up.
(Closes the notebook)
Someone like you must have everything under control, with nothing ever going wrong or deviating from plan.
I'm sure your life is smooth sailing. You'll never wake up one day only to find you've lost everything.
(Guzzles the drink)
(Rubs the mug nervously)
Not exactly...
Not exactly what?
No, my life has hardly ever been in my control.
(Takes a sip)
Poor thing.
Please don't say that.
I meant myself.
(Finishes in a single gulp)
Alright, I've got to go... Hey, where's my money? Oh, right, I gave you everything I had left.
I'll pick up the tab.
Thanks.
Why don't you take these gold coins? You'll need them.
Nah, I won't. Keep them.
You're drunk.
Don't worry about it, I can stand on my own. Farewell, friend.
♪I held her in my arms, before the day was gone♪
♪She smelled of jasmine, beneath the purple veil♪
♪Her soft lips take me away♪
♪To our eternal home far away♪
♪A moment of pain, for a lifetime♪
The drunk merchant staggers towards the rising sun, the great red orb on the horizon swallowing up his silhouette. He does not turn back, as though he is headed for his beloved's burning embrace.
The dry winds of the desert cover his song in a thin layer of sand, to be preserved for the next traveler.
♪Louisa, Louisa in my heart♪
♪Take me home with you, and I'll want nothing more♪
♪Louisa, Louisa in my dreams♪
I'm sorry, Totter, but we have to leave you here.
We're headed north, and there's no way you can keep up with that injury.
You'll just abandon me here?
This is near the Snow Realm. It's a beautiful place.
But you're still abandoning me here, right?
I'll leave some money for you. There's a village nearby where you can buy necessities.
Stop dodging the question! Answer me!
Totter, I...
Do you think the same, Ann?
Don't be like that. You know we can't slow down for you. We have our missions to complete.
So you're abandoning me.
You're not a child anymore. Throwing tantrums won't get you anywhere.
This isn't what we agreed on, Ann.
No one can predict the future, Totter... We might be back by next spring. Or things may have changed by then. Don't beat yourself up over it.
Ha. So will you come back for me?
...I see.
♪Louisa, Louisa in my heart♪
♪Take me home with you, and I'll want nothing more♪
♪Louisa, Louisa in my dreams♪
♪I'll always be there...♪
♪...Waiting for you♪
(Finishes in a single gulp)

The key. Where's the key?
Is it this one?
No, not this one.
This one?
No... forget it.
(Sits down)
...What time is it? Must be almost time. I'll wait outside.
The eaves of the roof casts a shadow on the hot sands, shielding Totter from the scorching sun.
Totter could not keep his eyelids open in the warm breeze.
He falls asleep, curled up against the door frame.
Totter! Totter! Wake up!
Hmnuh? ...Whoa! What is it?
I'm here to pick you up. Sorry about the delay; we ran into a sandstorm on the way. Hope we didn't keep you waiting?
(Stands up and brushes the dirt off his pants) No, you came just in time.
But you had fallen asleep.
Just a nap. I had to go out earlier.
Er... why are you smiling?
I'm smiling?
(Touches the edges of his mouth)
Strange. Why am I smiling?

recs.name: Homecoming
recs.tag: Nobody really lets life pass them by.

lines.x: It all started in the company bathroom. That day, I was sobbing uncontrollably on the toilet, overwhelmed by despair over my chaotic life.

Outside the stall, a few colleagues who had just returned from a trip to Sargon were chatting about their vacation. From their conversation, I overheard a name and a profound theory that helped me calm down.
And so I packed my bags and traveled from the steel jungles of Columbia to the dense rainforests of Sargon, braving countless hardships along the way. Eventually, I arrived here and met the sage.
Welcome to the Sanctuary. So, did you meet the sage today?
I did. It was truly an honor. Even though it was quite late, he still listened patiently to my questions and shared his wisdom.
What did he say?
Nothing. He just coiled the rope in his hands, without saying a word.
...Rope?
Yes. He was trying to show me my troubles were like tangled threads: if I just have enough patience, I can untangle them to be weaved into sturdy ropes.
And those ropes will rest neatly in my palm. They will no longer cause me any headaches.
That... makes sense. The sage is as wise as ever.
Of course, you're also very perceptive, to be able to grasp the sage's wisdom so quickly.
Yes. Before I left, he gave me a long, contemplative look. I think he was praising me, in his own way.
Yes. I think you're right.
To be honest, at first I thought this whole 'spiritual journey' thing was all just a rumor.
No. We follow the sage. He has never led us astray.
I think I'll sleep soundly tonight.
Then go sleep. Tomorrow's sermon will start at 8:00 A.M. sharp. I will be there to escort you all to the lecture hall.
...Each person walks through their life alone.
Like a solitary boat drifting on a lake...
The sage sits cross-legged on a massive rock in the lake beneath the waterfall, calmly sharing insights gained from observing the flowing water with the crowd gathered on the shore.
The crowd listens intently, letting his gentle words seep into their hearts.
Hello, friend. When did you arrive?
Just yesterday. How about you? How long have you been here?
Almost a month now. Hard to believe, right? Just a month ago, I was still stuck in the shadow of my last relationship, completely dejected.
But you look positively enlightened... Oh, I get it. It's because of the sage.
Yes. He led me out of the pain and darkness.
Hearing the chatter from the crowd, the sage pauses for a moment, gazes into the distance, and smiles warmly at everyone.
Shh. The sage is looking my way! I...
The sage's gaze is so warm. All my pain and suffering just melt away under it.
As I look into his eyes, so full of compassion, understanding, and detachment, I can finally find harmony with everything around me.
Everything that happens to us is but like flowing water...
All will flow away, and all will pass.
Look! He's reaching out towards us. That's his signature move!
Shh! He's gonna say it! This is my favorite part!
Say what? What's the sage going to say?
Just wait a minute, and you'll find out.
Ask nothing from life...
Let the river take me where it will!
Wooooah.
Totter, you stopped in the middle for a little bit. Why?
I heard someone's voice in the crowd, so I stopped to take a look.
Oh? Who was it? Which of them weren't paying attention?
I don't know. I wasn't wearing my glasses, so I couldn't see.
Tch... Can we find a new location for the next sermon? There are too many mosquitoes here by the water.
Ahem, there won't be a next one. According to our script, you're about to step out of the spotlight.
About time...
Thanks to you, we've made a fortune off of these tourists over the past few months.
*sigh* If only we hadn't been dead broke these past few years, we wouldn't have bothered a sick person like you.
It's fine. Being away from my hometown for so long and coming back empty-handed... I have to admit, I do feel a little guilty. So I'm glad I can help.
After all, it was the villagers who pooled the money for my travel expenses after my father passed. Now it's my turn to repay their kindness.
I must admit, I feel a bit embarrassed for disturbing the peaceful final chapter of your life.
I didn't expect saving that tour group would bring so much trouble. No idea what they said when they got back that brought all these people here...
At first, I thought someone important had come to the village.
When I listened to their story, I realized they were looking for you. Back then I just wanted to play along and make a little in the process.
So, you were already planning to rip them off?
I just told them what they wanted to hear. It takes effort and skill to speak to people's emotions. So what if I charge them a little for it?
(Narrows eyes)
Compared to those psychiatrists in the nomadic cities, it's practically pocket change.
Why did you return the money I gave you, anyway? It was quite a lot. There's really nothing you want to buy?
Not a thing. I just want to live out the rest of my days in peace and tranquility.
As long as you embrace the flowing river, you will find your way to the distant horizon.
...Isn't that from tomorrow's script?
Ha. Seems like you've already memorized your lines.
My time working together with the sage was indeed short.
After spending half a month in the rainforest, he suddenly announced to everyone that he was leaving to embark on a new journey to somewhere entirely new.
He announced his own death.
Hello, sir. Has there been an emergency?
I'm just as clueless as you are. All I know is the sage told me to gather everyone here.
What? Why didn't you tell us earlier? I'm still in my pajamas. I can't go see him wearing this.
Worry not, for the sage does not care about such trivial matters.
Good. Oh look...
A few hornbeasts slowly walk out of the rainforest, stopping by the waterfall. A few seconds later, more animals walk out, settling at the riverbank.
A fin leaps out of the water, but the ripples it creates do not disappear.
Immediately, everyone realizes that the river and the waterfall are frozen in place. In fact, they stopped flowing some time ago.
The sage slowly makes his way out from behind the curtain of water, clad in plain clothing.
Fellow travelers. I am sorry to keep you waiting.
As soon as he starts speaking, the river starts flowing again.
The sage!!!
Hey! Hey! Stop shoving your way to the front!
I have to get closer to him, so he can see how much I support him!
Sage, the sun has only just risen. What do you wish to tell us?
Last night, while exploring the jungle, I saw starlight filtering through the gaps in the leaves, falling onto the surface of the lake, and I...
*sigh*... Fellow travelers...
It was there I saw that my days are nearing their end. I called you all here today, to bid you farewell.
Surely you're joking, dear sage?
Nonsense. The sage never tells jokes!
Sage, does this mean you can see your own future?
The past and the future are just two segments of the same river. As long as we are in the river, we can decipher the messages from the future that come with those ripples.
But glimpsing into one's own destiny comes at a price. I can feel this place rejecting me; my journey in this world is nearing its end.
Sage, how can you be so indifferent in the face of death?
I accepted my fate long ago. I have found my inner peace.
Fellow travelers, do not weep for me. For me, death is but the start of a new journey.
Wow. I see the tranquility in your face. It's clear as day...
I have long come to terms with everything I've experienced, just as the river embraces everything that flows into it and continues its journey toward the distant horizon.
Sage, before you leave us, can you tell us how to interpret all of this?
It is not my place to reveal those hidden secrets.
Farewell, fellow travelers...
A fowlbeast lands on the sage's shoulder. He closes his eyes and lowers his chin, as if in some kind of trance.
The current surges beneath his feet, creating a whirlpool.
The water splashes violently. In the blink of an eye, the sage disappears into the vortex.
Only a small whirlpool is left, quietly spinning on the surface of the water.
In Columbia, I was a failure. I was dead broke, and my family was on the verge of breaking up. But this trip has given me the courage to face life again.
The sage's calm acceptance of his own fate has convinced me that there will always be a river to carry away the pain I've endured.
Odd... this isn't where we agreed on.
Can't trust the guy to dig a proper escape ditch.
Sage?
The river flows.... as the sands of time...
Enough. I already know what's going on here.
You won't tell anyone, will you?
Did you know? I happen to be a Sarkaz mercenary.
Uhh... Relax, If I wanted to tell anyone, I would've done so a long time ago.
From the very first day I arrived, I sensed something was off—simplistic platitudes like that rarely resonate with anyone.
But I never saw anyone complain.
Why would we?
The scenery is beautiful, the food is excellent, and to be honest, you looked quite striking in your 'Sage' getup.
Most important of all, the cost of living here is pretty reasonable. For us, it was the perfect place to spend a vacation.
But every time I spoke, you guys all seemed so invested in what I was saying. Like, true believers.
Meh. I treated it as cosplay, or maybe dinner theater. I saw a similar performance in Lungmen once. Only that time, the guy was dressed up as a gangster.
I've never been to Lungmen.
You should go some time. It's nice.
I don't think I'll get the chance.
Don't worry. No one's going to call you out.
Everyone comes here for a brief respite, a temporary escape from the troubles of real life. Who cares about the truth?
In the end, we will all return to our own rivers.
Just as the sage says.
Yeah, just as the sage says. Our thoughts and troubles remain in our respective rivers.
Totter, you know... if you want to stay at the office, you can. Rhodes Island has a great hospice program.
Thanks, but I'd rather live out my days back in my hometown.
But didn't you say you couldn't contact your family?
Yeah, because they're all dead.
Then you want to return home to live alone?
Yup. Great, isn't it?
Great how?
It's peaceful alone.
Having other people around pitying me would only be a pain.
Here, some dry clothes. Put them on.
What took you so long?
...It's quite a ways from the waterfall to here. You couldn't find me a shortcut?
Our other plan was to have you disappear in a flock of fowlbeasts. The problem with that one was you'd end up covered in poop.
Okay, you made the right choice.
I just hope that once I'm gone, my 'grand finale' will be enough to keep drawing a steady stream of tourists.
To be honest, the rainforest is huge. There must be somewhere you can stay and rest. You don't need to leave.
I promise that future visitors will not disturb your peace. We'll also pay for your food and clothing. If you need anything, just say the word.
No. I still plan on leaving.
Maybe everyone else sees me as a slick talker, but we grew up together—you know I wouldn't lie to you.
I know. I'm not stupid.
...Then why?
The sage is right. I should find my own river, the tranquil river that will embrace me and carry me onward.
Aren't you the sage?
No. I was just pretending to be him.
Everything he said, I made it all up, Totter. It's all beastshit.
Doesn't matter. I've always gone with the flow anyway.
It doesn't matter whether the sage is 'real' or not.
What matters is that we all have our trials and tribulations. The day we accept that is the day we shall find true peace.
I think I'm ready to face my future again.
It's been over six months since Totter returned to his hometown. In another six months, let's find some time to visit him together.
Hey... that's...
Totter?!
...Some stuff happened. Change of plans.
Huh?
Anyway, I'm back now.
So now you're planning to... uhh... I don't know what to think.
Oh good, now that you're back, I won't need to hunt you down in the rainforest. I've got a letter for you.
Huh? ...For me?
From where?
The snowfields.
That's strange...
Who sent it?
Uhh... probably some old friends.
